research_mode: official Department for Transport accredited statistics; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.name: Fatality road-user mix
verified_claims: In 2025, 41% of fatalities were car occupants, 25% motorcyclists, 24% pedestrians and 5% pedal cyclists.
limitations: Road-user shares do not locate incidents.

sources.name: Car-occupant fatalities
limitations: National totals cannot be assigned to a parcel without geocoded collision evidence.

sources.name: Pedal-cycle fatalities
limitations: Small annual changes may not represent a durable trend.

sources.name: Goods-vehicle occupant fatalities
verified_claims: Goods-vehicle occupant fatalities were 44 in 2025, 10% lower than 2024.
limitations: This is an occupant category and not a freight-route safety score.

sources.name: All-casualty road-user mix
verified_claims: In 2025, 53% of casualties were car occupants, 16% pedestrians, 12% motorcyclists and 13% pedal cyclists.
limitations: Category shares are national and not exposure-adjusted for a specific place.

sources.name: Car-occupant casualties
verified_claims: Car-occupant casualties declined 3% to 67,720 in 2025, the third consecutive annual decline.
limitations: The trend does not establish safety at a specific road or parcel.

sources.name: Pedestrian casualties
limitations: The total is provisional and lacks parcel-level denominator data.

sources.name: Motorcycle casualties
limitations: Total casualties and fatalities can move differently and should not be conflated.

sources.name: Goods-vehicle occupant casualties
verified_claims: Goods-vehicle occupant casualties increased 11% to 4,647 in 2025.
limitations: Vehicle-occupant counts do not identify collision hot spots.

sources.name: Bus or coach occupant casualties
verified_claims: Bus or coach occupant casualties declined 9% to 2,036 in 2025.
limitations: National public-transport occupant totals are not local accessibility or safety measures.
